title: Claude for teams: a 5-day playbook to get a whole team using Claude
summary: Ruben lays out a Monday-to-Friday plan to get a team actually using Claude: build one Project per recurring deliverable, add prompt templates, manufacture a before/after "wow", convert one overloaded teammate, then roll out with seeded DMs. The core idea is that adoption is a sales and context problem, not a training problem.

principles.text: Build a separate AI Project per recurring deliverable, each with only the context that task needs.
principles.quote: Each Project gets only what it needs (in terms of context).

principles.text: Remove the blank-chat problem: give teammates a one-sentence, single-input prompt template and let Project instructions carry the rest.
principles.quote: The template should rely on the Project instructions for everything else — tone, format, quality, guardrails. Don't repeat any of it in the template.

principles.text: Adoption comes from a specific output that makes people feel behind, not from features. Manufacture that proof with a real before/after.
principles.quote: People don’t adopt tools because of features. They adopt tools because someone showed them a specific output that made them feel behind.

principles.text: Treat adoption as a sales problem: convert one overloaded colleague using their own real work, then let others follow.
principles.quote: Adoption is a sales problem. Get one colleague excited, and the rest will follow.

principles.text: Pick the person who is drowning for your first conversion, not the tech enthusiast or the biggest skeptic.
principles.quote: The person who is **drowning**. Behind on emails. Always in meetings. Staying late.

principles.text: The first interaction decides whether someone keeps using a tool, so pre-configure the workspace and seed rollout with personal DMs.
principles.quote: The first interaction someone has with an AI tool determines whether they use it again.
